title: The String Quartet
objective: After this level you can explain what a string quartet is and why composers loved writing for it.
summary: A string quartet is two violins, a viola and a cello: one player per part, no conductor. Haydn developed it into a conversation among equals, and Mozart dedicated six quartets to him.

cards.headline: Four players, no conductor, nowhere to hide.
cards.body: A string quartet is just two violins, a viola and a cello, with nobody out front waving a baton. In 1785, after hearing six new quartets by Mozart, Haydn paid him an extraordinary compliment. Why did the great composers love this tiny group so much?

cards.headline: Four equals in conversation
cards.body: Chamber music usually has one player to a part and no conductor, and the string quartet became its star: from about 1750 it was chamber music's main medium, largely thanks to Haydn, known as the Father of the String Quartet. The Classical quartet was an intimate dialogue among equals. Goethe later described it as "four rational people conversing."

cards.headline: Why composers loved it: nowhere to hide
cards.body: With four players, every line is exposed. The Classical quartet was tightly built and challenging to play, and Haydn's Opus 33 quartets and Mozart's six quartets for Haydn became the model later quartets were measured against for a long time. Compare Level 36's swelling orchestra, with a conductor out front. A quartet has one player per part and nobody in front, so the four keep themselves together.

mascot.line: Imagine being handed the cello part at a party where Haydn and Mozart are also playing.

cards.headline: Haydn and Mozart: the quartet friendship
cards.body: In the 1780s Haydn and Mozart played quartets together, Haydn on violin and Mozart on viola. In 1785, after hearing six new quartets by Mozart, Haydn told Mozart's father, Leopold, that Wolfgang was the greatest composer he knew, in person or by reputation. Mozart dedicated all six to Haydn, an unusual gesture, since dedications usually went to wealthy patrons. So much for jealous rivals.

options.rationale: Leopold heard Haydn's praise; the dedication went to Haydn.

options.rationale: Level 38's alleged villain got no dedication here.

options.rationale: Dedications usually went to patrons, which made this one unusual.
